trial_name.text: Combined analysis of Studies MCD-501, MCD-201, and MCD-202 (treated cohort) versus untreated natural history control (Study MCD-502)

citations.quote: The results of Studies MCD-201, MCD-202, MCD-501, and MCD-502 provided the primary basis to establish the efficacy and safety of fosdenopterin for the treatment of MoCD Type A.

Efficacy was assessed in a combined analysis of the 13 patients with genetically confirmed MoCD Type A from Studies MCD-501, MCD-201, and MCD-202 who received substrate replacement therapy with Nulibry (or rcPMP).

phase.text: Phase 2 (Study MCD-201); efficacy derived from pooled clinical trials plus a retrospective observational study and a natural history control

citations.quote: Study MCD-201 is an ongoing prospective, open-label, single arm, phase 2 study intended primarily for the patients with MoCD Type A enrolled in Study MCD-501 (described below) to transition from treatment with rcPMP to fosdenopterin.

design.text: Nonrandomized, uncontrolled, open-label treated cohort pooled from two clinical trials and a retrospective observational study, compared to a matched untreated external (natural history) control cohort

citations.quote: Evidence of a survival benefit with fosdenopterin is based on an analysis of data pooled from a cohort of treated patients from two clinical trials and a retrospective observational study compared to a matched observational cohort of untreated patients; this constitutes an adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation.
Despite the limitations resulting from the lack of randomization, the use of an external noncontemporaneous control group, and the use of retrospective observational data in the treatment cohort

population.text: Neonatal and pediatric patients with genetically confirmed MoCD Type A

citations.quote: A total of 13 neonatal and pediatric patients with MoCD Type A was treated across the three Studies MCD-501, MCD-201, and MCD-202.

endpoint.text: Overall survival, comparing the treated group to an untreated natural history control cohort

citations.quote: The SAP specified using the log-rank test to compare treated and natural history control patients and using Kaplan-Meier (KM) plots and methods to estimate survival parameters for each group, including OS rates at 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years.

indication.text: NULIBRY is indicated to reduce the risk of mortality in patients with molybdenum cofactor deficiency (MoCD) Type A.

citations.quote: NULIBRY is indicated to reduce the risk of mortality in patients with molybdenum cofactor deficiency (MoCD) Type A.

target_moa.text: Fosdenopterin is a chemically synthesized form of cyclic pyranopterin monophosphate (cPMP) that provides an exogenous source of cPMP; cPMP is converted to molybdopterin and then to molybdenum cofactor (MoCo), restoring MoCo biosynthesis (deficient in MoCD Type A due to MOCS1 mutations) and thereby MoCo-dependent enzyme activity such as sulfite oxidase.

citations.quote: Nulibry is a chemically synthesized form of endogenous cPMP. It treats MoCD Type A by replacing the cPMP substrate and permitting the remaining MoCo synthesis steps to proceed, enabling activation of MoCo-dependent enzymes and the elimination of sulfites.
Fosdenopterin provides an exogenous source of cPMP. cPMP is converted to molybdopterin, which is then converted to molybdenum cofactor (MoCo) and restores molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis.

modality.text: Small molecule (chemically synthesized cyclic pyranopterin monophosphate; substrate replacement therapy)

citations.quote: Origin Biosciences, Inc. (Origin) submitted this new drug application (NDA) 214018 for Nulibry (fosdenopterin, a chemically synthesized form of cyclic pyranopterin monophosphate or cPMP), seeking approval of this first-in-class substrate replacement therapy for the rare disease molybdenum cofactor deficiency (MoCD) Type A.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>25%): catheter-related complications (89%), pyrexia (78%), viral infection (56%), pneumonia (44%), otitis media (44%), vomiting (44%), cough/sneezing (44%), gastroenteritis (33%), diarrhea (33%), bacteremia (33%). Potential for photosensitivity based on nonclinical phototoxicity.

detail.text: No companion diagnostic; genetic testing confirms MoCD Type A but no FDA-cleared companion test is required. Start if known or presumed MoCD Type A; promptly discontinue if not confirmed by genetic testing.
